### Resolving DaVinci Resolve Surface Tracker Crashes

Based on your system specifications and the specific crash scenario involving the Fusion Surface Tracker, the issue likely stems from a conflict between the software, GPU driver, and system configuration, especially when processing demanding 4K Blackmagic RAW media. The following checklist provides a systematic approach to isolate and resolve the instability.

### Systematic Diagnostic Checklist

This checklist is ordered from in-application tweaks to deeper system-level changes. Test the crash condition after each major step.

| Step | Category | Action | Details |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | **Media Test** | Isolate the BRAW Clip | Transcode a short segment of the 4K BRAW clip to ProRes 422 HQ. Apply the Surface Tracker to this new file. If it doesn't crash, the issue is related to BRAW decoding. |
| 2 | **Resolve Prefs** | Change BRAW Decode | Go to `Preferences > System > Memory and GPU`. Under GPU Configuration, uncheck "Use GPU for Blackmagic RAW decode". This forces CPU decoding and can bypass a GPU-specific bug. |
| 3 | **Resolve Cache** | Use Proxies | In the Media Pool, right-click the BRAW clip and select "Generate Proxy Media". Ensure playback is set to use proxies (`Playback > Proxy Handling > Prefer Proxies`) and try the tracker again. |
| 4 | **Windows Setting** | Disable HAGS | Go to `Windows Settings > System > Display > Graphics > Change default graphics settings`. Turn off **Hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling** and restart your PC. This feature can cause instability in pro apps. |
| 5 | **NVIDIA Panel** | Set Max Performance | Open the NVIDIA Control Panel, go to `Manage 3D Settings > Program Settings`. Select DaVinci Resolve (`resolve.exe`) and set "Power management mode" to "Prefer maximum performance". |
| 6 | **Driver Version** | Try an Alternate Driver | Use DDU in Safe Mode to uninstall the current driver. Install a slightly older (e.g., 537.42) or the absolute latest NVIDIA Studio Driver. A specific version may have a bug affecting Fusion. |
| 7 | **System Stability** | Disable XMP/Overclocks | Reboot into your BIOS/UEFI. Temporarily disable any CPU overclocking and the XMP/DOCP profile for your DDR5 RAM, letting it run at its default JEDEC speed. Memory instability is a common cause of silent crashes. |
| 8 | **Software Version** | Update DaVinci Resolve | Your issue might be a known bug in version 18.5. Check the Blackmagic Design support page for a newer stable version (e.g., 18.6 or higher) which may contain a fix. |

### Quick Actions

If the issue persists, generating diagnostic logs is the most critical step for getting official support.

- Action: [Button: Generate Resolve Logs] From DaVinci Resolve's top menu, navigate to `Help > Create Diagnostics Log on Desktop`.
- Action: [Button: Visit Support Forum] Post your issue and the diagnostic log on the official Blackmagic Design forum for expert review. <https://forum.blackmagicdesign.com/viewforum.php?f=21>

### Sources

- Official DaVinci Resolve Support: <https://www.blackmagicdesign.com/support/family/davinci-resolve-and-fusion>
- NVIDIA Studio Driver Downloads: <https://www.nvidia.com/download/find.aspx>
